ai.description: Minervarya cepfi is a small frog (25–30 mm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale yellow belly. It is distinguished by a distinct mid-dorsal stripe and a prominent, shovel-shaped inner metatarsal tubercle.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya cepfi* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, and prominent white mid-dorsal stripe running from the snout to the vent.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya cepfi* inhabits the Western Ghats, typically found in high-altitude (above 1,000m) montane evergreen forests, grasslands, and marshy areas near streams.
ai.behavior: The CEPF Burrowing Frog is primarily nocturnal and remains buried in moist soil during the day to avoid desiccation, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya cepfi* is an explosive breeder that lays clutches of 200–400 eggs in temporary rain pools during the monsoon season (June–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya cepfi* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically occurring in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 700 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Minervarya cepfi* produces a high-pitched, insect-like trill consisting of rapid, repetitive pulses, typically heard from flooded paddy fields or marshy grasslands.
